title: Compatibility of the Kunneth map with Leray, proper base change and the projection formula
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, let $f:X\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $g:Y\to S$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base]. Put $W=X\times_S Y$, with projections $p:W\to X$, $q:W\to Y$ and $c=fp=gq$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

(a) Assume that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, let $E\in D^+(X_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ have torsion cohomology [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], and let $K\in D^+(Y_{\Et},\mathbf Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

(b) Alternatively, let $n\ge1$ be invertible in $k$, set $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, let $Y$ be of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be arbitrary, possibly unbounded.

In either case use ordinary derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor] and unbounded derived global sections [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]; identify the derived category of module sheaves on $S_{\Et}$ with $D(\Lambda)$ by evaluation at $S$. Put
$$A=R\Gamma(X_{\Et},E),\qquad B=R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K),\qquad F=p^{-1}E,\qquad T=F\otimes^L_\Lambda q^{-1}K.$$
Let $\sigma_{U,V}:U\otimes^L_\Lambda V\xrightarrow{\sim}V\otimes^L_\Lambda U$ denote the canonical symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. Identify $g^{-1}A$ with the constant complex $\underline A$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf], [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. Write
$$e:g^{-1}A\longrightarrow Rq_*F$$
for the canonical exchange morphism [def-kun-unbounded-exchange],
$$t=\mathrm{PF}_q(F,K):Rq_*F\otimes^L_\Lambda K\longrightarrow Rq_*T$$
for the projection-formula morphism [def-kun-projection-formula-map], and
$$r=\mathrm{PF}_{Y,\Lambda}(K,A):B\otimes^L_\Lambda A\longrightarrow R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline A)$$
for the constant-coefficient projection morphism [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. Let
$$\ell:R\Gamma(W_{\Et},T)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*T)$$
be the canonical Leray composition comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. All these maps are computed in the full unbounded derived categories; bounded-below isomorphism assertions in (a) are interpreted through their canonical inclusions.

The arrows $e,t,r$ are isomorphisms: in (a) their isomorphism assertions are respectively [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below], [lem-kun-0f0f], [lem-kun-0f0e]; in (b) they are respectively [lem-kun-0f0c], [lem-kun-0f0g], [lem-kun-0f12]. Define the composite
$$\begin{aligned}
\theta:R\Gamma(W_{\Et},T)
&\xrightarrow{\ell} R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*T)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,t^{-1})}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},Rq_*F\otimes^L_\Lambda K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,e^{-1}\otimes1)}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},\underline A\otimes^L_\Lambda K)\\
&\xrightarrow{R\Gamma(Y,\sigma_{\underline A,K})}R\Gamma(Y_{\Et},K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline A)\\
&\xrightarrow{r^{-1}}B\otimes^L_\Lambda A
\xrightarrow{\sigma_{B,A}}A\otimes^L_\Lambda B.
\end{aligned}$$
Then $\theta\circ\kappa_{E,K}=1_{A\otimes^L_\Lambda B}$ for the canonical Kunneth map [def-kun-kunneth-map]; consequently $\kappa_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\theta$.

proof.text: Work with a fixed commutative coefficient ring, and write $L_u=u^{-1}$, $R_u=Ru_*$. The derived adjunctions and their units and counits are those explicitly specified in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. By [lem-kun-0ezp], every etale $S$-scheme is a disjoint union of copies of $S$. The sheaf axiom gives $H(\coprod_I S)=\prod_I H(S)$, with restriction maps given by the maps of index sets. Thus evaluation $H\mapsto H(S)$ and the constant-sheaf functor [def-kun-constant-sheaf] are inverse equivalences, also for module sheaves: the module action is evaluated componentwise. The equivalences are exact, so applying them to complexes and inverting quasi-isomorphisms gives the asserted derived identification. In particular $R_fE=A$, $R_gK=B$, $L_gA=\underline A$; the last identification also follows from [lem-kun-pullback-constant]. The ordinary adjunction for $g$ becomes the constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunction of [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism] under this equivalence: a map $\underline M\to H$ is determined by the images in $H(Y)$ of its constant labels, and conversely these sections restrict to define the map on each etale object and then its sheafification. This is the same Hom bijection as $g^{-1}\dashv g_*$, since evaluating $g_*H$ at $S$ gives $H(Y)$. The tensor comparisons in both descriptions send a pair of constant labels to their tensor, so they agree before deriving. Computing both Hom bijections on the same K-injective representatives identifies their derived counits and tensor comparisons as well. Let $\ell:R_cT\to R_gR_qT$ be the composition comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. It is compatible with the composite adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], not just an unspecified isomorphism of objects. Indeed [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] show that for a K-injective representative $I$ of $T$, $q_*I$ is K-injective. Choose $J=q_*I$ and $j=1$ in the normalization of that composition lemma: $\ell$ is then the ordinary composition identification on complexes. The units and counits are induced by the same ordinary adjunctions, whose composite counit is $\varepsilon_q\circ L_q\varepsilon_g$ by the cited composite-adjunction definition. Hence transposing through $\ell$ is exactly transposing first under $L_g\dashv R_g$ and then under $L_q\dashv R_q$, with $L_qL_g\cong L_c$. The composition identifications on inverse images used here are the canonical module lifts of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], clause (2). That statement explicitly says that they carry the composite-adjunction unit to the single-map unit under the direct-image composition identification. Hence the ordinary-composition normalization just checked also identifies the single-map derived adjunction with the composite one, with no choice of an unrelated isomorphism of left adjoints. These are exactly the composition identifications specified in the current [def-kun-kunneth-map].

proof.text: Use $\otimes$ for $\otimes^L_\Lambda$. We will suppress the canonical comparisons $L_u(U\otimes V)\cong L_uU\otimes L_uV$ of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], but check their compatibility with composition and symmetry. For the canonical module composition maps of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], clause (2), either order of successive inverse images sends a local pure tensor $x\otimes y$ to the tensor of the two successively pulled-back labels. The inverse-image composition identification therefore respects the two tensor factors; the two maps agree on local generators, hence on sheaves. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives using the equivalence in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. By [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] the constant-coefficient module pullback $u^*$ is canonically $u^{-1}$ and is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], its termwise application preserves K-flatness and flat terms; exactness preserves the chosen resolution quasi-isomorphisms. The original models and all their successive pullbacks therefore compute the derived tensors by [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the canonical comparison is the ordinary comparison in every bidegree. The same local-label calculation applies to the square isomorphism $L_qL_g\cong L_pL_f$: each route pulls back each of the two labels along the equal composite $c$. The symmetry multiplies bidegree $(i,j)$ by $(-1)^{ij}$, which is unchanged by inverse image and by composition. Both routes have differential $d\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d$. Thus the equations hold on these models. The two-variable determination of natural transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] extends these equations to the full derived categories. This proves precisely the tensor/composition and tensor/symmetry identifications used below; it does not infer them from an exchange-pasting theorem. The symmetry is the canonical one of [lem-kun-tensor-sym].

proof.text:
Define $s:A\otimes B\to R_g(L_gA\otimes K)$ by
$$s=R_g(\sigma_{K,L_gA})\circ r\circ\sigma_{A,B}.$$
By [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism], the $g$-adjoint of $r$ is $\varepsilon_{g,K}\otimes1_{L_gA}$. By the adjunction identification in step 1 this is the $g$-adjunction used here. Naturality and involutivity of the signed symmetry checked in step 2 give the explicit equality
$$\sigma_{K,L_gA}(\varepsilon_{g,K}\otimes1_{L_gA})\sigma_{L_gA,L_gB}=1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K}.$$
Thus [lem-kun-tensor-sym] and the adjunct-counit identity give
$$\varepsilon_{g,L_gA\otimes K}\,L_g(s)=1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K}.$$
For $F=L_pE$, the definitions [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and [def-kun-projection-formula-map] give, respectively,
$$\varepsilon_{q,F}L_q(e)=L_p(\varepsilon_{f,E}):L_qL_gA\cong L_pL_fA\to F,$$
$$\varepsilon_{q,T}L_q(t)=\varepsilon_{q,F}\otimes1_{L_qK}.$$
Each equality is just the adjunct-counit identity [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], applied to the specific adjoint written in the cited definition; all source tensor identifications are those checked in step 2. No map is assumed invertible in these equalities.

proof.text:
Put $U=L_gA\otimes K$, $m=t\circ(e\otimes1_K):U\to R_qT$, and
$$v=R_g(m)\circ s:A\otimes B\longrightarrow R_gR_qT,\qquad \lambda=\ell^{-1}\circ v.$$
Naturality of the counit for the morphism $m$ says
$$\varepsilon_{g,R_qT}\,L_gR_g(m)=m\,\varepsilon_{g,U}.$$
Consequently the $g$-adjoint of $v$ is $m(1_{L_gA}\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K})$, by step 3. The composite-adjunction formula [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and the normalization checked in step 1, make the $c$-adjoint of $\lambda$ the following typed morphism:
$$L_qL_g(A\otimes B)\xrightarrow{L_q(1\otimes\varepsilon_{g,K})}L_qU\xrightarrow{L_q(e\otimes1)}L_q(R_qF\otimes K)\xrightarrow{L_qt}L_qR_qT\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{q,T}}T.$$
This is obtained by applying the Hom bijections, whose inverse is the counit formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity]; no unit is moved past a tensor without the naturality already checked.

proof.text:
Substitute the projection identity from step 3 into this $c$-adjoint. Bifunctoriality of the tensor comparison [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] turns its final two arrows into $\varepsilon_{q,F}\otimes1_{L_qK}$. Composing with $L_q(e\otimes1)$ and the first arrow then gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\lambda^\flat
&=(\varepsilon_{q,F}L_qe)\otimes L_q(\varepsilon_{g,K})\\
&=L_p(\varepsilon_{f,E})\otimes L_q(\varepsilon_{g,K}):
L_c(A\otimes B)\cong L_pL_fA\otimes L_qL_gB\longrightarrow L_pE\otimes L_qK=T.
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is the exchange identity from step 3. To compare with the current [def-kun-kunneth-map] without suppressing its source comparisons, write $\mu^c_{A,B}:L_cA\otimes L_cB\xrightarrow{\sim}L_c(A\otimes B)$ and use that definition's $\gamma_{f,p}:L_c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_pL_f$ and $\gamma_{g,q}:L_c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_qL_g$. The preceding computation says explicitly that $\lambda^\flat=(L_p\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes L_q\varepsilon_{g,K})\circ(\gamma_{f,p,A}\otimes\gamma_{g,q,B})\circ(\mu^c_{A,B})^{-1}$. The module composition maps in steps 1-2 are precisely these $\gamma$ maps, and the tensor comparison is the inverse of the same canonical $\mu^c$. This is exactly the $\alpha_{E,K}$ whose adjunct defines $\kappa_{E,K}$ in [def-kun-kunneth-map], using the same K-injective Hom bijection and ordinary counits as in step 1. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection therefore proves $\lambda=\kappa_{E,K}$. In particular this argument works for all commutative coefficient rings and unbounded complexes; properness and finiteness are needed only to make its factors invertible.

proof.text: For (a), $q$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability]. The exact additive inverse image of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] carries bounded-below $E$ to bounded-below $F$. It also carries torsion sheaves to torsion sheaves: with the kernel/filtered-colimit definition [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf], exactness identifies $L_p(H[n])$ with $(L_pH)[n]$, and left adjointness identifies $L_p(\varinjlim_n H[n])$ with $\varinjlim_n L_p(H[n])$. The latter assertion follows directly by applying the adjunction to the colimit universal property: maps out of either object are compatible families of maps from $H[n]$ to the right adjoint. Thus $F$ has torsion cohomology. The hypotheses of [lem-kun-0f0f] hold for $(q,F,K)$ and make $t$ invertible. The hypotheses of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below] hold for $(f,g,E)$ and make $e$ invertible, using the same canonical mate as in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For this last identification, [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction] normalizes the bounded derived counit on a bounded-below injective representative by the termwise ordinary counit. The unbounded adjunction in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] has the same normalization. The Hom bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] computes both on the same representatives, so the bounded exchange of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] and the restriction of the unbounded exchange have equal transposes $L_p\varepsilon_f$; hence they agree. To apply the constant projection lemma, $A$ is bounded below: [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] give a bounded-below K-injective representative $I$ of $E$, and [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded] computes $A$ by $\Gamma(X,I)$, whose terms have the same lower bound. Now [lem-kun-0f0e] applied on the assumed qcqs $Y$, to $K$ and the constant coefficient complex $A$, makes $r$ invertible. The definition of that canonical map is [def-kun-constant-projection-morphism]. The comparison $\ell$ is invertible on the entire ambient derived category by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], so no additional tensor boundedness theorem is needed to use Leray here.

source.place: etale-cohomology.tex Tags 0F14 (lemma-kunneth-one-proper), part (1), 0F0F (lemma-projection-formula-proper), 0F0E (lemma-pull-out-constant); proper base change as cited in the item

proof.text: For (b), again $q$ is proper by [lem-kun-proper-stability], and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$ is a torsion ring since $n1_\Lambda=0$. Thus [lem-kun-0f0g] applied to $(q,F,K)$ makes $t$ invertible without boundedness conditions. The unbounded proper base change statement [lem-kun-0f0c] applies to $(f,g,E)$ and makes $e$ invertible. The affine singleton $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: its coordinate ring has only the ideals $(0),(1)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], the finite-type scheme $Y$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], it is also quasi-separated. Since $k$ is separably closed, clause (2) of [lem-kun-0f10] gives $\kuncd(Y)<\infty$. Apply [lem-kun-0f12] on $Y$, to $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $A\in D(\Lambda)$, to conclude that $r$ is invertible. No finite Tor amplitude or boundedness is required of either object. The entire unbounded Leray comparison $\ell$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. This is the same derived composition arrow as the finite-cohomological-dimension Leray presentation in the imported statement. The stated invertibility of $n$ in $k$ is retained, although these one-proper-factor inputs do not need it.

In both cases the morphisms $s,e,t,\ell$ are isomorphisms by steps 6 and 7 and the symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym]. The symmetry squares to the identity: on bidegree $(i,j)$ the two signs multiply to $(-1)^{ij+ji}=1$, first on the tensor models and then by the descent argument of step 2. Therefore
$$s^{-1}=\sigma_{B,A}\circ r^{-1}\circ R_g(\sigma_{L_gA,K}).$$
Reverse the displayed factorization $\lambda=\ell^{-1}R_g(t)R_g(e\otimes1)s$. Its inverse is
$$\lambda^{-1}=s^{-1}R_g(e^{-1}\otimes1)R_g(t^{-1})\ell,$$
which, after substituting the preceding formula for $s^{-1}$, is exactly the stated $\theta$. Functoriality and tensor bifunctoriality take inverse pairs to inverse pairs, so cancellation gives $\theta\lambda=1$ and $\lambda\theta=1$. Step 5 identifies $\lambda$ with $\kappa_{E,K}$, proving both the required identity and the isomorphism assertion. Notice that the adjoint being compared was that of $\lambda:A\otimes B\to R_cT$, not that of $\theta\kappa:A\otimes B\to A\otimes B$.

split_report.blueprint: The imported sole proof paragraph is realized by steps 1-2 (derived/monoidal identifications), 3-5 (three explicit adjunct identities and the common c-adjoint), 6-7 (separate hypothesis audits of parts (a)/(b)), and 8 (inverse cancellation). The geometric route remains Leray, projection formula, proper base change, constant projection, symmetry.

tool_uses.why: Its normalized composition comparison on all ordinary unbounded module derived categories identifies the successive transposes and supplies Leray without an extra boundedness premise on the tensor; it does not replace the proper-base-change/projection-formula route.
Exactness and the sheaf-level module adjunction ensure that the actual constant-coefficient pullbacks preserve boundedness and torsion; the unit monoidality lemma alone does not state this.
K-injective preservation lets the normalized unbounded composition comparison be computed with the identity replacement, checking its compatibility with the composite adjunction.
Its uniqueness of extension from flat-term K-flat models promotes the explicit tensor/composition and tensor/symmetry calculations to arbitrary derived objects.
The general adjunct/counit formula evaluates the three specific canonical maps; this is categorical bookkeeping, not another Kunneth theorem.
Its explicit normalization of bounded units and counits checks that the bounded proper-base-change theorem concerns the same exchange mate used in the unbounded calculation.
Its Hom bijection identifies the bounded and unbounded counits computed on the same bounded-below injective representatives, so equal transposes identify the exchange maps.
Supplies the category hypothesis for a bounded-below injective representative used to check A belongs to D+ in the constant projection theorem.
